Variants.Content: The Old Gods have no High Patriarch, Book of Books, or Unified Temple; worshipers pray before weirwood heart trees, in sacred groves, and in ancient lands. A few ancient families in the North and the Riverlands and the ancestors of the valley retain this belief, handing over oaths, deaths, marriages and family memories to the tree with the face carved on it. Followers of the Seven Southern Gods often think that the Old Gods are silent and distant, while believers of the Old Gods may feel that there are too many bells in the temple and the gods are too human-like. The power of faith in the old gods is not in preaching, but in the land, ancestors and the private testimony of others who do not need it.
